Subject: Hosting region confirmation + VPC options for SIG/CAIQ

Hi Rishi,

As part of our vendor SIG/CAIQ review and upcoming SOC 2 documentation, we need explicit confirmation about where customer data is hosted and how private deployments are handled. Specifically: 

- Can you confirm that HelixHealth customer data for our account will be hosted and persist only in US regions (no EU/APAC replication) unless we opt into multi-region?
- For private deployments: do you support a VPC peering model or a private endpoint (customer-managed VPC with private link)? We need an outline of network controls and an estimated lead time to provision a private deployment in our AWS account.
- Is there an auditable attestation or signed letter Redwood can provide stating region commitment and isolation guarantees we can include in procurement?

Our SOC 2 attestation review kicks off 2026-12-01; if you can get us the confirmation + runbook by next week that would be ideal. I’ve included Samir (CISO) on this thread.

Thanks,
Amelia Turner
Head of Vendor Risk

Amelia — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Jordan (solutions) and Mina (security) to provide the technical and compliance artifacts.

Quick answers up front:
- Yes — for your account we can restrict persistent storage and model hosting to US-only regions (we don’t enable cross-region replication unless explicitly requested in writing).
- We support both customer-managed VPC peering and private endpoints (private link) depending on your networking preference. Each has tradeoffs which Jordan will outline.
- We can provide a signed hosting attestation letter and an evidence pack mapped to SIG items. Jordan/Mina — can you assemble the runbook + signed letter and a short timeline for provisioning a private deployment in HelixHealth’s AWS account (assume standard security review/access granting)?

I expect an internal delivery of artifacts within 48 business hours. If Helix needs a DocuSign for the attestation, we’ll include that.

Best,

Hi Amelia / Rishi — here are the technical details and attachments I pushed to the Drive link below. Attaching short stubs here as well.

Summary (short):
- Region: We will provision model-serving instances and persistent storage in the US-East-1 or US-West-2 regions only for this account. No replication to EU/APAC unless you opt-in via a signed change order.
- Network options:
  1) VPC Peering (customer-managed VPC): Redwood launches a private endpoint in our partner subnet and we establish VPC peering. Pros: low latency, direct routing. Cons: cross-account peering permissions required and route table changes on Helix side.
  2) Private Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink): We expose a private endpoint service; Helix creates Interface VPC Endpoints in your VPC. Pros: simpler to grant access, no route table changes. Cons: slightly higher per-ENI cost.
- Key management: We support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) for data-at-rest; HSM-backed keys via AWS CloudHSM can be integrated for the private deployment.
- Provisioning timeline: Typical lead time is 5–8 business days after we receive completed access request + signed attestation (provisioning ticket: INFRA-4398).

Attachments (referenced):
- vpc-connection-runbook-v2.md (network steps, example CloudFormation snippets)
- redwood-hosting-region-letter.pdf (draft attestation; we can DocuSign)
- sig-evidence-pack.zip (mapping files: SIG->artifact list, CAIQ pointers)

Hi Amelia — adding a couple compliance clarifications for your SIG/CAIQ mapping: 

- Data residency: For the HelixHealth tenant we will enforce a hard region tag at provisioning time. That tag drives our placement service and prevents accidental scheduling to other regions. We will provide a signed PDF attesting to that behavior (redwood-hosting-region-letter.pdf).
- Logging / audit: All admin and infra-level logs for the tenant are retained in US regions and are exported to your chosen S3 bucket on request for audit; retention policy is configurable.
- Encryption: Data at rest encrypted with AES-256. We will use customer-managed KMS keys if requested; we support per-tenant KMS key partitions. 
- SIG/CAIQ evidence: The attached sig-evidence-pack.zip maps SIG control IDs to artifacts (SOC 2 report references, network diagrams, access review receipts). A couple of items in SIG require Helix to acknowledge your own network hardening steps (we call these shared-responsibility items) — I flagged those in the mapping.

Next steps I propose: 1) Jordan prepares runbook + provisioning ticket; 2) we issue the signed attestation and route to procurement via DocuSign; 3) provision private endpoint after Helix shares the access request spreadsheet.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
